answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. The key insight is that coordination itself leaks: the more unified a farm is, the more easily its shared style or timing betrays it. In effect, the network makes cheating the most expensive strategy available, which is the closest thing to a Sybil-resistant design that economics allows. Consider a falcon as the anchor of the cost.
